name: fig_runtime_dist
title: Runtime distributions
question: How long does each stage of a CryoLean check take, how variable is it, and where does a full check spend its time?
model: Wall-clock timing (time.perf_counter) of repeated calls interleaved in random order; violins are Gaussian KDEs of log10(time); boxes are IQR and median. The breakdown uses timing wrappers around the calls verifier.check makes (lean_runner.check, lean_runner.axiom_audit, smt.*), behaviour unchanged.
data: paper/data/bench_runtime_dist.json and paper/data/fig_runtime_dist.json, written by paper/scripts/fig_benchmarks.py; 40 repeats per row after 2 warm-up rounds. Pairs: MET = mat_magnetometry_vsm/qd_dynacool_14T_eto_vsm_hc, NOT MET = mat_magnetoresistance_10T/qd_dynacool_9T_eto_res (Demo A), NEED INFO = mat_magnetoresistance_10T/qd_dynacool_14T_eto_vsm_hc; batch = all 286 pairs of the 11 x 26 grid in one check_batch. Verdicts re-computed by Lean in every repeat. Machine: Intel(R) Core(TM) i9-14900HX (24 cores / 32 threads, 29.7 GiB), Windows-11-10.0.26200-SP0, Python 3.12.10, cryolean v2 (Lean 4.35.0), Z3 5.3.3.
caption: Distributions of 40 interleaved repeats of each stage. A single Lean check costs about one process start (210 ms for the MET pair), batching the 286-pair grid brings it to 2.5 ms per pair, and a Z3 conflict explanation takes 11 ms. A full check with suggestions takes 367 ms to 1.59 s; panel (b) attributes it to the Lean verdict, Z3 suggestions, Lean re-checks of the five suggested alternatives (one process each), and the verdict card's axiom-audit freshness test, which re-hashes the 107 MB checker binary on every check. All values are measured; every repeat's verdict came from Lean. The machine was not idle: median whole-system CPU utilisation during this benchmark was 36% (other desktop applications, antivirus scanning and other sessions' jobs).
